row_factor.hf_formula: Huynh-Feldt epsilon with Lecoutre's (1991) correction, ((N - g + 1) d GG - 2) / (d (N - g - d GG)), capped at 1 (as R car and afex)
row_factor.note: Mauchly's test is reported, not used to choose the correction: P is Geisser-Greenhouse corrected either way.
row_factor.mauchly_note: With 2 levels there is one contrast, so sphericity always holds (epsilon = 1).

interaction.hf_formula: Huynh-Feldt epsilon with Lecoutre's (1991) correction, ((N - g + 1) d GG - 2) / (d (N - g - d GG)), capped at 1 (as R car and afex)
interaction.note: Mauchly's test is reported, not used to choose the correction: P is Geisser-Greenhouse corrected either way.
interaction.mauchly_note: With 2 levels there is one contrast, so sphericity always holds (epsilon = 1).

interaction_contrasts.p_adjustment: none (each contrast is its own question)
interaction_contrasts.error_term: the subjects' contrast scores, variance pooled across the 2 groups (df = 12 subjects - 2 groups)
interaction_contrasts.source: Maxwell & Delaney 2004, Designing Experiments and Analyzing Data, 2nd ed., ch. 12-14 (contrasts in within-subject and split-plot designs, each with its own error term); Gelman & Stern 2006, Am Stat 60:328
notes: 2 x 2 design: this contrast's t^2 is the interaction F and its P the interaction P
interaction_contrasts.explainer: To ask whether the effect of one factor differs between the levels of the other, look at the interaction: the difference of the two effects with its CI. One effect being 'significant' and the other 'not significant' does not show that they differ (Gelman & Stern 2006).

contrast_notes: The contrasts and simple effects of a repeated-measures design are tested on the subjects' contrast scores, variance pooled across the 2 groups (df = 12 subjects - 2 groups), not on the pooled ANOVA residual, so they need no sphericity.
